name: Festival Gate
read: Inside the gate, the trampled path opens into a small clearing walled by corn taller than a rider. A little wooden ticket booth leans to one side, and a painted festival sign lies face down in the straw beside a child's dropped lantern. Carved jack-o'-lanterns grin from the ground, lit by candles that should have burned out hours ago. Paths lead away north and south into the dark corn.
notes:
The entrance of the maze. The Hollowmere Harvest Festival began here every year: guests paid at the booth and walked into the corn. On festival night the corn grew over the festival grounds and the maze closed behind them. The jack-o'-lanterns give orange light; the rest of the maze is dark.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in the cash drawer of the ticket booth, among the festival tickets.

Exits: Scarecrow Row (3, opening in the corn), Crow Field (2, opening in the corn). The opening in the north side leads straight on to Scarecrow Row; the opening in the south side leads straight on to the Crow Field. The entrance gate in the east side leads back out to the farm lane.

name: Crow Field
read: Black feathers cover the straw of this wide clearing like a fallen blanket. A food cart lies on its side, spilling apples and corn cobs, and three cloaked people lie still beside it. A broken scarecrow pole leans over them, and from the corn all around comes a low, dry rustling and the clicking of many beaks.
notes:
Festival-goers fled here when the corn closed in. The crows found them first. The crows serve the walking scarecrows and the Harvest Witch, and they keep watch over the southern paths.

Encounter (Power Level 8, Durability 15)

Five Murder Crow Swarms burst out of the corn when the first creature reaches the middle of the clearing. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in the belt pouch of one of the dead festival-goers.

Exits: Festival Gate (1, opening in the corn), Rotten Gourd Patch (4, gate), Hay Bale Fort (5, gate), Lantern Clearing (6, gate). The opening in the north side leads to the Festival Gate. The opening in the west side leads to a path with a gate north into the Rotten Gourd Patch and a gate south into the Hay Bale Fort. The opening in the east side leads to a path that ends at a gate into the west side of the Lantern Clearing.

name: Scarecrow Row
read: Eight scarecrows stand on wooden poles in two loose rows across this clearing, their burlap faces turned toward the path. Straw hats sit low over stitched eyes, and their arms hang from crossbars with wisps of straw stirring in the night air. A wheelbarrow and a few garden tools lie beside a heap of spare straw. There is no wind.
notes:
Four of the eight scarecrows are ordinary. The other four are Scarecrow Stalkers. While a Stalker stays still, it looks exactly like an ordinary scarecrow; a DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check made within 10 feet notices fresh mud on its feet.

Encounter (Power Level 9, Durability 18)

Four Scarecrow Stalkers stand among the four ordinary scarecrows. They wait until most of the party is between the rows, then step down from their poles and attack. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Festival Gate (1, opening in the corn), The Thresher (7, barred iron gate), Scarecrow Shrine (14, gate), Rotten Gourd Patch (4, open path), Burned Wagon (8, gate), Farmer's Grave (9, gate), Hollow Placard (12, opening in the corn). The opening in the south side leads to the Festival Gate. The opening in the west side leads to a path that reaches a barred iron gate into The Thresher to the north-west; past it, the path climbs a wooden stile over a fence and runs on west to the Scarecrow Shrine and south to the Rotten Gourd Patch. The opening in the east side leads to a path with a gate south into the Burned Wagon and a gate north into the Farmer's Grave; the path continues east to the west side of the Hollow Placard.

name: Rotten Gourd Patch
read: Swollen gourds and pumpkins lie in a tangle of vines across the middle of this small clearing. Their skins are grey-green and furred with black mould, and some have split open. A cracked watering can lies at the edge of the patch. The air is thick and sweet with rot.
notes:
The witch's blight took this patch first. The gourds are full of black spores.

Trap: Rotten Gourd Patch

  • Trigger: a creature steps into the patch of gourds in the middle of the clearing.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices the gourds swell and shrink slowly, as if breathing, and the black dust around the split ones.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition until it finishes a Short Rest.
  • Disarm or avoid: Walk around the patch along the edge of the clearing, or burn the gourds from at least 10 feet away with any fire; the fire destroys the spores.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Hay Bale Fort (5, gate), Crow Field (2, opening in the corn), Scarecrow Shrine (14, gate), The Thresher (7, barred iron gate), Scarecrow Row (3, opening in the corn). The gate in the south side opens onto a short path with a gate south into the Hay Bale Fort and a way east to the Crow Field. The open way in the west side leads to a long path west to the Scarecrow Shrine; a branch climbs north over a wooden stile to The Thresher and Scarecrow Row.

name: Hay Bale Fort
read: Small square straw bales are stacked in a ring in this clearing, with one gap for a doorway. Inside the ring sit a wooden prize chest, a toy wooden sword, a straw doll and an empty burlap sack. The bales are scuffed with small boot prints, but no child's voice answers.
notes:
The children's fort of the festival. The prize chest held the prizes for the festival contests: the prize purse for the best harvest and a straw hat for the best costume. The chest is closed but not locked.

No encounter.

Treasure: 300 gp (the festival prize purse) and the Scarecrow's Straw Hat (the costume prize) in the prize chest.

Exits: Rotten Gourd Patch (4, gate), Crow Field (2, gate), Root Cellar Hatch (15, gate). The gate in the north side opens onto a short path with a gate north into the Rotten Gourd Patch and a way east to the Crow Field. The open way in the west side leads to a long path west that ends at a gate into the Root Cellar Hatch.

name: Lantern Clearing
read: A dozen carved jack-o'-lanterns stand in a ring in this clearing, some on the ground and some on short wooden posts, all burning with orange light. A carving table holds knives and heaps of pumpkin pulp, and seeds are spilled across the ground. Some of the lanterns are turning slowly to face you.
notes:
The carving tent of the festival stood here. When the witch stole the Harvest Ember, its sparks fell into the carved pumpkins, and some of them woke as Lantern Gourdlings. The lanterns give orange light across the clearing.

Encounter (Power Level 10, Durability 16)

Four Lantern Gourdlings rise from among the ordinary jack-o'-lanterns and float into the air, spitting burning seeds. They fight until destroyed.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Crow Field (2, gate), Bobbing Barrel (11, opening in the corn), Witch's Cauldron (10, gate). The gate in the west side opens onto the path to the Crow Field. The opening at the east end of the north side leads to the Bobbing Barrel, and the gate in the south side opens into the Witch's Cauldron.

name: The Thresher
read: An old wooden threshing machine stands in this small clearing, its iron crank and row of curved blades red with rust. Piles of cut cornstalks and broken boards lie around it, and a sack beside the blades is stained dark. Something small and pale glints among the boards.
notes:
Farmer Jack Hollow's threshing machine. The corn grew around it on festival night, and the witch's magic now drives it. The glint among the broken boards is a necklace, lost by the festival's Harvest Queen when she fled.

Trap: The Thresher

  • Trigger: a creature steps into the clearing in front of the blades.
  • Find: DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) notices fresh cut marks in the ground in a wide arc in front of the machine, and that the crank is not rusted to its axle.
  • Effect: DC 16 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 slashing]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam the blades with an iron bar, a crowbar or a polearm (DC 16 Strength (Athletics)), or crawl along the edge of the clearing behind the machine.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Ivory Harvest Necklace among the broken boards.

Exits: Scarecrow Row (3, barred iron gate), Scarecrow Shrine (14, barred iron gate), Rotten Gourd Patch (4, barred iron gate). The barred iron gate in the south side opens onto a path; an iron bar across it lifts out without a check. The path runs south-east to Scarecrow Row, and south over a wooden stile to the long path to the Scarecrow Shrine and the Rotten Gourd Patch.

name: Burned Wagon
read: The black frame of a burned hay wagon stands in this clearing on broken wheels, and ash and burnt straw cover the ground. A charred body in a breastplate lies beside it, one hand still on a small sack. The husks of the corn around the clearing are moving, though there is no wind.
notes:
The body is a sellsword the festival hired to keep order. He set the hay wagon alight to hold back the creatures of the maze; the fire burned him with it. The corn husks here have knotted together into Husk Stranglers. The breastplate is burned through and is of no use.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 18)

Three Husk Stranglers tear free of the corn walls when a creature enters the clearing. They grapple the nearest creatures and fight until destroyed. They avoid the burned ground around the wagon.

Treasure: a Potion of Climbing in the sack of rations beside the body.

Exits: Farmer's Grave (9, gate), Scarecrow Row (3, gate), Hollow Placard (12, gate). The gate in the north side opens onto the path east of Scarecrow Row. North across that path is the gate into the Farmer's Grave; west is Scarecrow Row; east the path runs to the Hollow Placard.

name: Farmer's Grave
read: A plain wooden coffin lies half sunk in an open grave in the middle of this clearing. A rapier lies across its lid, and a shovel stands upright in a mound of dark earth beside a small wooden marker. The soil around the grave looks freshly turned, and it is very cold.
notes:
The grave of old Amos Hollow, Jack's father, a soldier in his youth who was buried with his rapier. The Harvest Witch dug him up to take his bones for her cauldron, but the dead of the Hollow family will not give him up.

Trap: Grave Hands

  • Trigger: a creature steps up to the open grave or touches the coffin.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices finger bones pushing up through the turned soil around the grave.
  • Effect: DC 15 Strength saving throw [[/save str 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 necrotic]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, held by the grave hands until it or an ally uses an action and succeeds on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
  • Disarm or avoid: Sprinkle holy water on the grave, or lift the rapier from at least 10 feet away with a pole, a rope or mage hand.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Rapier +1 on the coffin lid.

Exits: Burned Wagon (8, gate), Scarecrow Row (3, gate), Hollow Placard (12, wooden stile). The gate in the south side opens onto the path east of Scarecrow Row, across from the gate into the Burned Wagon. The open way in the east side leads to a path that crosses a wooden stile and ends at the north side of the Hollow Placard.

name: Witch's Cauldron
read: A large black iron cauldron bubbles over a small fire in the middle of this clearing, and its green glow lights a ring of stones, hanging bundles of dried herbs and corn husk dolls, and bones beside a wooden stool. A hunched old woman in a shawl of corn husks stirs the pot, with two scarecrows standing at her back. In the east side of the clearing stands a tall wooden gate, bound in iron and shut.
notes:
Mother Gristle, the Harvest Witch, tends the maze from here. She made the bargain with Jack Hollow and took his head on festival night. The cauldron gives green light across the clearing. The gate in the east side is the locked gate to the Hollow King's Clearing (room 13). The Iron Harvest Key from the Scarecrow Shrine (room 14) opens it. The lock can also be picked (DC 18 Dexterity check with thieves' tools) or the gate forced open (DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check).

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 17.5)

The Harvest Witch and two Scarecrow Stalkers. The witch is an Epic commander: she gives orders to the Stalkers and fights from behind them, using her wand to hold attackers in webs. While the Harvest Witch lives, a Scarecrow Stalker that drops to 0 Hit Points in this clearing rises again at the start of her next turn with half its Hit Points. Each Stalker can rise only once.

Treasure: a Wand of Web, the witch's own, carried in her belt.

Exits: Lantern Clearing (6, gate), The Hollow King's Clearing (13, locked gate). The gate in the north side opens into the Lantern Clearing. The locked gate is at the north end of the east side.

name: Bobbing Barrel
read: A large wooden barrel stands in the middle of this small clearing, full to the brim with black water. Red apples float on the surface and a few more lie on the ground beside a small wooden bench. A string of festival bunting lies in the straw. Something faint glows far down in the water.
notes:
The festival's apple-bobbing barrel. A festival-goer drowned in it on festival night, held under by the witch's magic, and the drowned face still waits in the water. The glow at the bottom is the light of a lantern.

Trap: Bobbing Barrel

  • Trigger: a creature steps up to the barrel or leans over the water.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices that the apples do not move when the barrel is touched, and a pale shape far below them.
  • Effect: DC 16 Wisdom saving throw [[/save wis 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 psychic]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.
  • Disarm or avoid: Tip the barrel over from at least 10 feet away with a pole or a rope, or cast dispel magic (DC 16) on it.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Lantern of Revealing at the bottom of the barrel.

Exits: Lantern Clearing (6, opening in the corn), Hollow Placard (12, opening in the corn). The opening in the south side leads to the Lantern Clearing and the opening in the north side to the Hollow Placard.

name: Hollow Placard
read: A wooden placard on a post stands at the centre of this clearing, painted with a crude face with hollow eyes and a wide grin. Torn festival bunting hangs from it, and a small pile of pumpkins sits at its foot beside a broken lantern. A tangle of husks in the corn wall shifts as you look at it.
notes:
The placard once showed the way to the festival's prize table. The witch's servants painted over it with the face of the Hollow King.

Encounter (Power Level 11, Durability 18.5)

One Husk Strangler, two Lantern Gourdlings and one Scarecrow Stalker. The Stalker stands still as an ordinary scarecrow beside the placard, the Gourdlings sit among the pumpkins, and the Strangler waits in the corn wall. They attack together when the party enters, and fight until destroyed.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in the pile of pumpkins at the foot of the placard.

Exits: Bobbing Barrel (11, opening in the corn), Farmer's Grave (9, wooden stile), Burned Wagon (8, gate), Scarecrow Row (3, opening in the corn). The opening at the west end of the south side leads to the Bobbing Barrel. The open way in the north side leads to a path over a wooden stile to the east side of the Farmer's Grave. The opening in the west side leads to a path west with gates into the Burned Wagon and the Farmer's Grave, and on to Scarecrow Row.

name: The Hollow King's Clearing
read: At the heart of the maze, a throne of straw bales and twisted cornstalks stands against the east side of the clearing, ringed by a heap of small carved pumpkins. Hoofprints are scorched black into the ground among scattered bones and a glittering pile of coins and festival prizes. On a black horse with burning hooves sits a headless rider, and on his shoulders burns a great carved pumpkin, its orange fire pouring out through the eyes and mouth.
notes:
The end of the adventure. The rider is the Hollow King: Jack Hollow's headless body, risen to rule the maze. His jack-o'-lantern head is lit by the Harvest Ember, the festival's hearth-fire, which the witch stole and set in the pumpkin. The Ember lights the clearing with orange fire. Behind the throne, wooden steps lead down to the farmhouse root cellar; the adventure does not go there.

Encounter (Power Level 12, Durability 18)

The Hollow King and two Lantern Gourdlings. The Hollow King is an Epic Boss and fights mounted on his nightmare horse, which is part of his stat block: he never rolls initiative, acts on initiative count 10, and takes one Response after each player character's turn. The Gourdlings rise from the heap of pumpkins around the throne.

Plucking the Ember. A creature within 5 feet of the Hollow King can use an action to pull the Harvest Ember from his head with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. On a success the King takes [[/damage 4d10 radiant]] and loses his Epic Boss Resistance for the rest of the fight. When the King dies, the Ember comes free on its own.

Treasure: The Harvest Ember (story item; in the King's head), the Flame Tongue Longsword the King fights with, and 600 gp in the pile of coins and prizes.

Exits: Witch's Cauldron (10, locked gate). The locked gate is in the west side. In the east side, behind the throne, wooden steps lead down to the farmhouse root cellar.

name: Scarecrow Shrine
read: A small wooden shrine stands in this clearing inside a ring of stones, and in it a crude carved scarecrow stares out with knotholes for eyes. Candles burn on a low table before it, among offerings of apples, corn and dried flowers. An iron key as long as a hand hangs from a hook on the front of the shrine.
notes:
The shrine where the witch's scarecrows and crows bring offerings to the Hollow King. The iron key is the key to the old farm gate that now closes the King's Clearing. The witch hung it here, trusting the far corner of the maze to keep it.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Iron Harvest Key (story item; it opens the locked gate between the Witch's Cauldron and the Hollow King's Clearing) on the hook.

Exits: Rotten Gourd Patch (4, gate), The Thresher (7, gate), Scarecrow Row (3, gate). The gate in the east side opens onto a long path east to the west side of the Rotten Gourd Patch. A branch of that path climbs north over a wooden stile to The Thresher and Scarecrow Row.

name: Root Cellar Hatch
read: A wooden hatch with a rusted iron ring is set flat in the ground of this clearing. Beside it, someone has dug a small hole, and the corner of an old iron strongbox shows in the earth next to a broken spade. Sacks of potatoes lean against the corn.
notes:
An old potato store of the Hollow farm. The hatch opens onto a small cellar that caved in long ago and holds nothing but earth. Jack Hollow buried his savings here in the bad years; the witch's servants began to dig them up and broke the spade. The strongbox is not locked.

No encounter.

Treasure: 500 gp in the farmer's buried strongbox.

Exits: Hay Bale Fort (5, gate). The gate in the east side opens onto a long path east to the west side of the Hay Bale Fort.
